skipped.reason: cannot occur in a two-player Forge game: every Forge card that says 'you get' an additional step or phase (Obeka, Splitter of Seconds; The Ninth Doctor) triggers only on its controller's own turn, Obeka on combat damage it deals as an attacker, and the attacking player is always the active player

scenarios.title: An effect lasting until a player's next upkeep expires as that upkeep begins

setup.notes: It is B's turn now and A's turn is next. During A's previous turn A activated Xenic Poltergeist targeting Sol Ring, so Sol Ring is a 1/1 artifact creature (power and toughness equal to its mana value 1) until A's next upkeep. Xenic Poltergeist is tapped from that activation and untaps in A's untap step.

decisions: B's turn ends: A and B pass in the end step, cleanup happens.
A's next turn begins: the untap step, in which A untaps Xenic Poltergeist, then the upkeep step begins and A would receive priority.
The board is observed at the point named by the variant; no other decisions are taken.

variants.label: at_upkeep
variants.expected: As A's upkeep begins, the animation effect has ended: Sol Ring is a noncreature artifact (no power or toughness) when A first receives priority in the upkeep step.

variants.label: in_untap_step
variants.delta: The board is observed in A's untap step, before the upkeep step begins.
variants.expected: Sol Ring is still a 1/1 artifact creature: A's upkeep has not begun, so the effect has not ended.

variants.label: poltergeist_is_Bs
variants.delta: Xenic Poltergeist is B's: B activated it targeting Sol Ring during A's previous turn, so the effect lasts until B's next upkeep.
variants.expected: Sol Ring is still a 1/1 artifact creature when A first receives priority in A's upkeep step: the effect waits for B's upkeep, not A's.

scenarios.forge_notes: Uses Duration$ UntilYourNextUpkeep. Check Forge removes the animation at the start of the upkeep step, not at the start of the untap step.

scenarios.title: Unspent mana empties from the mana pool as a phase ends

setup.notes: Omnath, Locus of Mana is a 1/1 that gets +1/+1 for each unspent green mana A has and lets A keep unspent green mana as steps and phases end. A has no spells to cast; the mana is simply left in the pool.

decisions: A taps Swamp for {B} and does not spend it.
A passes priority with an empty stack and B passes: the precombat main phase ends and the beginning of combat step begins.
The mana pool and Omnath's power and toughness are observed at the beginning of combat step.

variants.label: black_mana
variants.expected: The {B} left in A's pool is gone when the precombat main phase ended: A's mana pool is empty and Omnath is a 1/1.

variants.label: green_mana
variants.delta: A taps Forest for {G} instead of Swamp for {B}.
variants.expected: The {G} is still in A's mana pool at the beginning of combat step because Omnath says A does not lose unspent green mana, so Omnath is a 2/2.

scenarios.forge_notes: Omnath uses Mode$ UnspentMana; check Forge empties the pool at the end of each step and phase, not once per turn.

scenarios.title: An effect lasting until end of combat expires at the end of the combat phase, not when the end of combat step begins

setup.notes: Battering Ram has 'At the beginning of combat on your turn, Battering Ram gains banding until end of combat.'

decisions: A passes priority in the precombat main phase with an empty stack, B passes, and the beginning of combat step begins.
Battering Ram's beginning-of-combat trigger goes on the stack; both players pass and it resolves: Battering Ram has banding until end of combat.
A declares Battering Ram as an attacker against B; B declares no blockers; combat damage is dealt.
The end of combat step begins. Both players pass priority with an empty stack in the end of combat step, then the postcombat main phase begins.

variants.label: main2
variants.expected: In the postcombat main phase Battering Ram no longer has banding: the effect ended at the end of the combat phase. B took 1 combat damage (life 19).

variants.label: end_of_combat_step
variants.delta: The board is observed while A holds priority in the end of combat step, before the combat phase ends.
variants.expected: Battering Ram still has banding in the end of combat step: the effect lasts until the end of the combat phase, not the beginning of that step.

scenarios.forge_notes: Uses Duration$ UntilEndOfCombat. Check that Forge removes the keyword when the end of combat step ends and not when it begins.

scenarios.title: A beginning-of-upkeep trigger fires when the upkeep step begins and goes on the stack before anyone receives priority
decisions: The upkeep step begins; no one has received priority yet.
Juzám Djinn's trigger is put on the stack before A receives priority; both players pass and it resolves.

variants.label: own_upkeep
variants.expected: Juzám Djinn's trigger fired as the upkeep began and was on the stack when A first received priority; it resolves and deals 1 damage to A (life 19).

variants.label: opponents_djinn
variants.delta: Juzám Djinn is on B's battlefield instead of A's, so it is A's upkeep but not its controller's.
variants.expected: No trigger: the stack stays empty and both life totals stay at 20.

variants.label: opponents_turn
variants.delta: Juzám Djinn is A's but the active player is B, so it is B's upkeep.
variants.expected: No trigger: the condition 'your upkeep' is not met in B's upkeep, so the stack stays empty and A's life stays 20.

scenarios.forge_notes: Variant opponents_turn has B as active player (setup.active B).

scenarios.title: A beginning-of-first-main-phase trigger fires when the precombat main phase begins, not the postcombat one

setup.notes: Abstract Paintmage: 'At the beginning of your first main phase, add {U}{R}. Spend this mana only to cast instant and sorcery spells.' A has already drawn for the turn in this draw step.

decisions: A passes priority in the draw step with an empty stack and B passes: the precombat main phase begins.
The Paintmage's trigger is put on the stack before A receives priority; both players pass and it resolves.

variants.label: precombat_main
variants.expected: The trigger fired when the precombat main phase began and resolves: A has {U}{R} in the mana pool.

variants.label: postcombat_main
variants.delta: The phase that begins is A's postcombat main phase (setup.step end_of_combat, combat has just ended with no attackers declared), not the precombat main phase.
variants.expected: No trigger fired and A's mana pool stays empty.

scenarios.forge_notes: The Paintmage's trigger checks Phase$ Main1. In the postcombat variant the main2 phase begins.

scenarios.title: An extra turn is taken directly after the current turn and the most recently created extra turn comes first

setup.notes: All Islands untapped. Time Walk is a sorcery, Nexus of Fate an instant that also gives an extra turn, Counterspell an instant.

decisions: A casts Time Walk, tapping both Islands.
B's response is named by the variant (no response in the base).
Both players pass until the stack is empty; the precombat main phase and the rest of A's turn proceed with no further actions.

variants.label: time_walk_alone
variants.expected: Time Walk resolves. The turns that follow this one are: A (extra turn), B, A.

variants.label: nexus_after
variants.delta: After Time Walk resolves, A passes priority and B casts Nexus of Fate, tapping seven Islands; it resolves.
variants.expected: B's extra turn was created after A's, so it is taken first. The turns that follow this one are: B (extra turn), A (extra turn), B, A.

variants.label: nexus_in_response
variants.delta: B casts Nexus of Fate in response to Time Walk, tapping seven Islands. Nexus resolves first, then Time Walk.
variants.expected: Time Walk's extra turn was created last, so it is taken first. The turns that follow this one are: A (extra turn), B (extra turn), B, A.

variants.label: countered
variants.delta: B casts Counterspell on Time Walk, tapping two Islands.
variants.expected: Time Walk is countered and no extra turn is added. The turns that follow this one are: B, A.

scenarios.forge_notes: Nexus of Fate shuffles itself into its owner's library instead of going to the graveyard; this does not affect turn order.

scenarios.title: An effect that adds phases inserts them directly after the specified main phase

setup.notes: All lands untapped. A has no creatures; the phase order is the only thing observed.

decisions: A casts Relentless Assault in the precombat main phase, tapping four Mountains.
B's response is named by the variant (no response in the base).
Both players pass until the stack is empty and then pass priority in every following phase and step without taking any action.

variants.label: main1
variants.expected: Relentless Assault resolves. The remaining phases of the turn in order are: additional combat phase, additional postcombat main phase, combat phase, postcombat main phase, ending phase.

variants.label: main2
variants.delta: A casts Relentless Assault in the postcombat main phase instead (setup.step main2).
variants.expected: Relentless Assault resolves. The remaining phases of the turn in order are: additional combat phase, additional postcombat main phase, ending phase.

variants.label: countered
variants.delta: B casts Counterspell on Relentless Assault, tapping both Islands.
variants.expected: Relentless Assault is countered and no phase is added. The remaining phases are: combat phase, postcombat main phase, ending phase.

scenarios.forge_notes: Relentless Assault uses AddPhase with ConditionPhases$ Main1,Main2; check that casting it in main2 adds the phases after main2.

scenarios.title: An effect that adds a step inserts it directly after the specified step

setup.notes: Paradox Haze is an Aura on player A: 'At the beginning of enchanted player's first upkeep each turn, that player gets an additional upkeep step after this step.' It is controlled by A.

decisions: The untap step passes with nothing to untap; the upkeep step begins.
Paradox Haze's trigger and Juzám Djinn's trigger are put on the stack; A orders them with Paradox Haze's trigger resolving first, and both resolve.
A passes priority at the end of the first upkeep step with an empty stack, B passes; the additional upkeep step begins.
Any triggers go on the stack and resolve; A passes priority with an empty stack, B passes, and the draw step begins.

variants.label: haze_on_a
variants.expected: A gets an additional upkeep step directly after the first one, before the draw step, and Juzám Djinn triggers again at its beginning (Paradox Haze does not trigger again, it says 'first upkeep'). A takes 2 damage in total (life 18).

variants.label: haze_on_b
variants.delta: Paradox Haze enchants B instead of A.
variants.expected: A's upkeep is not B's first upkeep, so no step is added: A has only one upkeep step, Juzám Djinn triggers once, and A's life is 19.

scenarios.forge_notes: Paradox Haze uses AddPhase with ExtraPhase$ Upkeep.

scenarios.title: An effect that adds a step after a phase creates a phase that holds only that step

setup.notes: Obeka has menace and 'Whenever Obeka deals combat damage to a player, you get that many additional upkeep steps after this phase.' A's library holds enough cards that nothing is drawn from an empty library.

decisions: A attacks B with Obeka, Splitter of Seconds.
B declares blockers as named by the variant (no blockers in the base).
If damage assignment is needed, Obeka assigns its 2 damage to the first Grizzly Bears.
Combat damage is dealt, any triggers resolve, and both players pass priority in every following step without taking any action.

variants.label: unblocked
variants.expected: Obeka deals 2 combat damage to B (life 18) and its trigger gives A 2 additional upkeep steps after the combat phase. Each comes in its own additional beginning phase that holds only an upkeep step (no untap step, no draw step): Obeka stays tapped, A draws no extra card, and Juzám Djinn triggers twice (A life 18).

variants.label: double_blocked
variants.delta: Both Grizzly Bears block Obeka (menace allows two blockers).
variants.expected: Obeka deals no damage to a player (one Grizzly Bears dies, the other is undamaged; Obeka has 4 damage and survives). The trigger does not fire, no extra upkeep step occurs, and both life totals are 20.

scenarios.forge_notes: Obeka's AddPhase uses AfterPhase$ EndCombat and NumPhases from the damage amount; check that each added phase contains only the upkeep step.

scenarios.title: A skipped step is passed as though it did not exist, so nothing in it happens

setup.notes: Eon Hub: 'Players skip their upkeep steps.'

decisions: The untap step passes with nothing to untap.
The next step is the upkeep step: with Eon Hub on the battlefield it is skipped. The draw step follows.
A and B pass priority in the draw step.

variants.label: with_eon_hub
variants.expected: A's upkeep step is skipped: Juzám Djinn's beginning-of-upkeep trigger never happens and A's life stays 20; the draw step follows the untap step directly.

variants.label: no_eon_hub
variants.delta: Eon Hub is not on the battlefield.
variants.expected: The upkeep step happens, Juzám Djinn's trigger resolves and A's life is 19.

scenarios.forge_notes: Eon Hub is a BeginPhase replacement effect with Skip$ True.

scenarios.title: A skipped turn is passed as though it did not exist

setup.notes: All lands untapped. The turn order observed is that of the turns after this one.

decisions: A casts Meditate, tapping three Islands; B passes and Meditate resolves.
Both players pass priority in every remaining step of the turn and in later turns without taking any action.

variants.label: meditate
variants.expected: A draws four cards and skips A's next turn. The turns that follow this one are: B, B, A.

variants.label: no_meditate
variants.expected: Nothing is skipped and A draws no extra cards. The turns that follow this one are: B, A, B.
